exposure: living with a dog in the first year of life
outcome: Number of positive skin prick tests (SPT)
cohort: 692 children (496 Black and 196 White) enrolled in the WHEALS birth cohort study
finding: Living with a dog in the first year of life was associated with decreased odds of having at least one positive skin prick test and eczema, with the strength of these associations varying by delivery mode, race, and birth order.
mod_finding: The association between living with a dog and having at least one positive skin prick test was stronger in children born via caesarean section compared to those born vaginally.
followup_time: 2 years (for eczema and SPT), 3-6 years (for asthma)
